statements.quote: But if the only solutions you have, if the only solutions you allow yourself, are oral medications, you’re going to miss out on the most effective and safe treatments that exist.
statements.context: Section arguing that the mental health start-up boom funds telehealth-only, oral-medication-only care models. The author claims such models will miss the most effective and safe treatments, meaning in-person neuromodulation (SAINT TMS) and metabolic care (GLP-1 drugs, waist measurement). A general conditional claim about how oral-medication-only care models will perform.
statements.note: Borderline: a general conditional about care models rather than a dated call. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: But those things require another article all by themselves because they’re so important.
statements.context: Closing section on holistic care of patients with psychiatric illness. 'Those things' are nutritious food (a 'Farm-acy Benefit Manager' joke) and exercise plans. The author implies a future newsletter article on diet and exercise.
statements.note: Weak implied commitment to a future article in the author's own newsletter. Coder may mark CONTROL or drop.

statements.quote: Thanks, my proposed 2023 Nobel prize winner in medicine, Nolan Williams, M.D.
statements.context: Footnote 11, comparing the 0.2 effect size of Abilify augmentation with the 1.7 effect size of SAINT (Stanford neuromodulation therapy, commercialized by Magnus Medical). The author proposes Nolan Williams, the SAINT researcher, as the 2023 Nobel prize winner in medicine.
statements.note: Wish/advocacy, not a prediction that he will win. Restated in footnote 1 of the 2022-10-24 post.

statements.quote: Young people are busy building businesses to be acquired by Pharma. They’re not gonna turn around and decide that the entire Pharma business model is all wrong… that’s just crazy talk. That makes you sound like some sort of anti-psychiatry lunatic. You’re never going to get a company funded with that attitude.
statements.context: Footnote 13 on the What If Ventures fellowship and the 2000+ funded mental health start-ups. The author predicts that young founders will keep building companies to be acquired by pharma and will not challenge the pharma business model, and that a company with an anti-pharma-model stance will not get venture funding.
statements.note: Compound claim: founder behavior ('not gonna') plus a venture-funding generalization ('never going to').

statements.quote: A child psychiatrist reflects, in advance, about the next preventable mass shooting that will rock our nation to the core.
statements.context: Subtitle of the section 'Satire, as a Public Health Intervention', a pre-written news account dated 2022-07-18 and republished here. The author asserts that another preventable mass shooting will occur in the United States and will follow a predictable pattern.
statements.note: Satirical framing; the underlying expectation of another mass shooting reads as sincere.

statements.quote: From what we know about the shooter at this time, he spent weeks/months planning the attack, and we do know he purchased the assault rifle/s legally, as well as the hollow point bullets that caused such horrible wounds. These purchases were made despite his history of disturbing statements and threats, both online and in real life.
statements.context: Satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting. Predicted details: the shooter will have planned for weeks or months, will have bought assault rifles and hollow point bullets legally, and will have a prior history of disturbing statements and threats online and offline.
statements.note: Satire template written in past tense about a future event; sincere as an expectation of the pattern.

statements.quote: Yet again, high-capacity magazines allowed one young man, between the ages of 16 and 26, to take his isolation and rage and turn it into a storm of lead, against which the innocent victims stood no chance. The standoff with the police doubtless took more time given that he was also equipped with tactical body armor, which prevented even the armor piercing bullets of the hand guns of the responding officers from taking him down before more death and destruction could be caused. In the end, he either took his own life, or was shot by responding officers/well-armed heroes.
statements.context: Satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting. Predicted: the shooter will be a young man aged 16 to 26 using high-capacity magazines and tactical body armor, the police standoff will be prolonged, and he will die by suicide or be shot by responders.
statements.note: Satire template. Compound claim: weapon, body armor, shooter age range, shooter fate.

statements.quote: The young white man in question had a history of mental illness/suspicion of mental illness and had participated in violent video games/online message boards. He left a number of videos/a manifesto, posted immediately before the attack.
statements.context: Satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting. Predicted shooter profile: young white man, with a history or suspicion of mental illness, involvement in violent video games or online message boards, and videos or a manifesto posted immediately before the attack.
statements.note: Satire template; sincere as an expectation of the recurring pattern.

statements.quote: The close-knit community of whatever town or city this shooting happened in gathered near the sight of the violence afterwards, to leave handmade memorials to the dozen or so who died at the hands of the shooter. Parents of the fallen expressed their disbelief/their complete resignation over the predictable fact that their child could’ve been killed in this way: “It’s about time law makers do something, this killing is senseless, and we’ve had enough!” said one father.
statements.context: Satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting. Predicted: about a dozen deaths, handmade memorials, and parents demanding that lawmakers act. The following paragraph also predicts a local trauma doctor describing war-zone injuries and further deaths after the event.
statements.note: Satire template; numeric detail 'the dozen or so who died'.

statements.quote: This is America, and the NRA staunchly supports the reduction of gun violence through the addition of more guns into the hands of more good guys. If only a good guy with a gun have been present/had been more able to aim accurately/had more well armed officers been present, this tragedy could’ve been avoided. It’s about time we focus on the mental health crisis that is driving this violence and the lack of armed responders to dangerous mentally ill people.
statements.context: Satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting; the passage is the predicted statement of an NRA spokesperson. The author predicts the NRA will respond by calling for more armed 'good guys' and by blaming the mental health crisis and the mentally ill rather than firearms.
statements.note: Parody of an NRA statement; the logged claim is the author's prediction of the NRA's framing after the next shooting.

statements.quote: The republican governor of the state in which x city/town is located spoke on the steps of the capital: “This senseless tragedy highlights how fragile life is, and how much we need to blame the mentally ill and the broken system that cannot proactively identify them and target them with suppressive fire from the nearly 400,000,000 current firearms deployed throughout the United States.”
statements.context: Satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting; the passage is the predicted statement of the Republican governor of the affected state. The author predicts the governor will blame the mentally ill and a system that fails to identify them, not firearms. The 400,000,000 firearms figure is a present-tense aside.
statements.note: Parody of a governor's statement; the logged claim is the author's prediction of political framing after the next shooting.

statements.quote: This time, clearly, given the scope of the tragedy, it will be different, and meaningful change is definitely going to happen thanks to the actions of brave lawmakers representing this locality.
statements.context: Closing line of the satirical pre-written account of the next mass shooting. Read literally it predicts meaningful legislative change after the next shooting. The ironic, sincere reading is the opposite: the author expects no meaningful change in gun law after the next mass shooting.
statements.note: Ironic. The sincere forecast is the inverse: no meaningful gun-law change will follow the next mass shooting.

statements.quote: So my guess is that Neurowrap is probably a scam.
statements.context: Conclusion of a website-only review of the Neurowrap, a direct-to-consumer 'happy hormones' wearable a colleague asked about, contrasted with the Magnus Medical (SAINT) website. The author judges that the Neurowrap is probably a scam.
statements.note: Present-tense judgment of a product, logged for recall; no explicit future state is claimed.
